## Problem

A browser login can verify credentials before a concurrent reset/deletion and persist a session afterward, or recreate a removed session through a later save. This is a bounded child of #421, not the complete Firebase migration.

## Requirements and acceptance

- Validate the verified account and credential version when first persisting the regenerated Passport session; reject stale login with the existing generic response.
- Make rejected saves terminal and accepted subsequent saves update-only so reset/deletion cannot be undone by session resurrection; rollback leaves no durable authenticated session.
- Preserve integer principals, cookie format, restricted recovery, local registration/dev login and the current-session update exception; do not add blanket version checks to existing sessions.
- Maintain real Passport/Express and PostgreSQL race/rollback regressions plus session-store/route tests; cover the full seven-file PR442 scope. Firebase remains disabled.
- No live account reads/imports, Firebase activation/provisioning, credential changes, deployment or release. Full #421 remains open and unfinished.

## Implementation plan

Build on PR437 after PR431. Guard the first password-login session save and subsequent update-only persistence. Test both mutation/save orders and failure recovery; do not change parent branches. Existing implementation evidence stays in PR442; independent QA must reassess final issue/body/linkage before readiness.

## Implementing Codex task

Verified existing task ID: `01a10cfe-a79f-7198-9e8f-2b4dc6703031`. Shareable link unavailable through current tools.

## Implementing PR

[PR442](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/442). This PR implements only this checkpoint; #421 remains the nonclosing parent outcome.
